nodes.name: Polyfluorene backbone synthesis
nodes.procedure: TP (8.28 g), DF (0.777 g), MP (4.98 g), and DCM (18 mL) were added to a 200 mL three-neck flask with a mechanical stirrer. After that, TFA (4.8 mL) and TFSA (36 mL) were slowly added into the above solution under -3.2 °C, and the reaction proceeded at -3.2 °C for ~12 h. Finally, the viscous solution was poured into 1000 mL 1 mol L−1 NaOH solution and continued stirring for 48 h. Then, it was washed with DI water several times until neutral pH. The polymer was dried in an oven at 80 °C for 24 h to obtain poly(fluorene-co-aryl methylpiperidine) (PFAM-x).
nodes.source_text: TP (8.28×g), DF (0.777×g), MP (4.98×g), and DCM (18 mL) were added... dried in an oven at 80 °C for 24 h to obtain poly(fluorene-co-aryl methylpiperidine) (PFAM-x).

nodes.name: PFTP synthesis
nodes.procedure: PFAM (3.0 g) and iodomethane (3 mL) were dissolved in DMSO (30 mL), and the reaction proceeded at 25 °C under stirring for 24 h in a dark environment. The resulting solution was precipitated in 300 ml of acetone and washed with DI water thrice. Finally, the polymer was dried to obtain a light-yellow poly(fluorene-co-aryl piperidinium) polymer (PFTP).
nodes.source_text: PFAM (3.0×g) and iodomethane (3 mL) were dissolved in DMSO (30 mL)... Finally, the polymer was dried to obtain a light-yellow poly(fluorene-co-aryl piperidinium) polymer (PFTP).

nodes.name: CPFTP synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthesis route of poly(fluorene-co-aryl piperidinium) polymer(CPFTP) is similar to PFTP. The PFAM (1.0 g), K2CO3 (0.646 g), and VBC (0.238 g) were dissolved in DMSO (12 mL). The reaction proceeded at 25 °C under stirring for 24 h. Then, add 2 mL iodomethane and stir for another 24 h. The reaction solution was treated in the same way as PFTP.
nodes.source_text: The PFAM (1.0×g), K2CO3 (0.646×g), and VBC (0.238×g) were dissolved in DMSO (12 mL)... The reaction solution was treated in the same way as PFTP.

nodes.name: NiFe catalyst synthesis
nodes.procedure: 30.3 g NiCl2·6H2O and 8.11 g FeCl3 were dissolved in 50 ml and 25 mL DI water, respectively. Metal precursor solution (1 mL) was prepared by mixing 0.665 mL NiCl2 solution and 0.335 mL FeCl3 solution. The 2 M NaBH4 solution was freshly prepared by dissolving 0.378 g NaBH4 powder in 5 mL deionized water. Subsequently, 1 mL metal precursor solution was quickly injected into the prepared NaBH4 solution by stirring it at 25 °C. A large amount of black NiFe catalyst is rapidly generated, and a large number of bubbles are released. The stirring was maintained for about 1 min. After freeze-drying, the NiFe catalyst was obtained.

nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: The catalyst ink was fabricated using the synthesized ionomer and catalyst through a widely adopted ultrasonication probe method. During tip sonication... the welltransient dispersion process of aggregates facilitates localized ionomer cross-linking through thermal trigger, thereby immobilizing catalyst particles... For the preparation of the anode, NiFe or PtRu/C catalysts, solvent (IPA/DI = 4/1), and CPFTP/PFTP or PFBP ionomer solution (5 wt% in DMSO) were initially sonicated in an ice-water bath for 1 h to obtain a well-dispersed catalyst ink, the ratio of NiFe to ionomers is 9:1 and PtRu/C to ionomers is 3:1, respectively.

nodes.name: MEA anode electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: The catalyst ink was sprayed on 10×10 cm NiFe foam or carbon paper (Toray-H-060) to prepare anode GDE with a NiFe loading of 4.0 mg cm−2 and cathode GDE with a PtRu/C loading of 0.5 mg cm−2. All the GDEs in the spraying process were heated on the 60 °C hot plate and adsorbed on the vacuum adsorption table. After spraying, the anode electrode containing CPFTP ionomer was heated on the 60 °C hot plate for 2 h to convert the CPFTP@NiFe anode CL into cross-linked forms thoroughly.
